tasks.short: Work out the ingredients and supplies needed to prepare a recipe for a given number of portions.

steps.what: Supervisor gets the number of portions from the event order or production plan
Supervisor looks up the recipe card in the kitchen folder
Supervisor scales ingredients to the portions and rounds to pack sizes
Supervisor checks stock on hand for each ingredient and supply
Supervisor lists what to pull from stock and what to order
Chef checks the estimate for dishes with variable yields

tasks.design: Hold recipes as bills of materials with yields in the recipe system ({OTHER}), linked to supplier pack sizes and the stock module: entering portions (or importing them from the production plan or event order) scales the recipe, rounds to pack sizes and subtracts stock on hand. The result is a pull list and an order list the supervisor checks and the chef reviews for variable yields. Only dishes with a recipe record, about 70%, get this; for the rest the supervisor still looks up the card, calculates and checks stock by hand.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipe cards were paper or documents, so every scaling was spreadsheet arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe tools hold recipes as bills of materials, link supplier articles and prices, and connect to stock.
tasks.still_hard: Recipes must be entered and kept current; yields of fresh produce vary, and stock figures for perishables drift.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing this week's produce yields less, and judging a safety margin for an important event.

ambition.what: Every event and batch estimated from the recipe record, so purchasing matches real need instead of habit.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor checks estimates instead of computing them; the chef owns the recipe data.

reach.learn: Whether batch yields in the recipe record match what the kitchen gets.

evidence.claim: A recipe tool rolls ingredient prices up to portion cost and applies connected suppliers' price changes.
Scaling a recipe by portions and rounding to pack sizes is plain arithmetic once recipes are held as bills of materials.

assumptions: Boundary: from portions needed to pull and order lists; ordering is outside.

Input contract: recipe with ingredient, quantity per portion and yield, kept by the chef in the recipe system; pack sizes from supplier article data; stock on hand from the latest count in the stock module; portions from the production plan or event order; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Scenario: about 70% of dishes have a recipe record; the rest are estimated by hand.
Chef time is outside the supervisor's savings.
unknowns: How many recipes are recorded with yields today.
How current stock figures are between counts.
research_questions: How far do estimates from recipe records differ from actual use at events?

already_counted.description: Supervisor checks scaled quantities for dishes with unusual yields.
Supervisor checks the generated pull and order lists.

incremental.description: Supervisor enters missing recipes and corrects pack sizes.
Chef keeps recipe quantities and yields current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about half the dishes have recipe records and stock data is often stale; high: about 90% of dishes recorded with current stock.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide what to buy, order food and supplies from suppliers, requisition equipment, and check deliveries.

steps.what: Supervisor decides what to purchase from the shortage list and upcoming events
Supervisor compares prices and availability on wholesaler webshops or by phone
Supervisor places supply orders by webshop, e-mail or messaging
Supervisor fills a requisition for equipment above the budget limit
Restaurant manager approves the equipment requisition
Supervisor orders the approved equipment from the supplier
Supervisor checks deliveries and passes delivery notes to the office
Office administrator matches invoices with delivery notes

tasks.design: The stock module of the recipe system ({OTHER}) proposes orders from par levels, the production plan and events, priced from a contract price list per supplier; after the supervisor's review, orders go to integrated wholesaler webshops on the {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and the rest are sent as e-mail orders. Equipment above the limit goes through a {WORKFLOW} requisition the manager approves, and deliveries are ticked off on a tablet so the {ERP} can match invoices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were built from memory and sent by phone, e-mail and messaging to each supplier separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe and stock tools link to supplier webshops and price lists, and approval forms take minutes to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Small and local suppliers take orders only by phone or message; choosing quality and substitutes is judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplier delivers good produce on time and deciding when quality beats price.

ambition.what: Contract prices checked against each order, so price creep is caught every week.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor reviews proposals and handles exceptions; the manager approves equipment from a form.

reach.learn: Whether chefs' special orders can use the same proposal and price list.

evidence.claim: A recipe tool applies connected suppliers' price changes to recipe costs.
Stock tools can turn par levels and planned production into order proposals sent to supplier webshops.
Food businesses need a HACCP plan; checking suppliers and deliveries is part of showing compliance.

assumptions: Boundary: from deciding needs to deliveries checked; invoice payment is outside.
Input contract: par levels set by the restaurant manager; production plan and event orders from their own tasks; contract prices per article kept by the manager; fallback is ordering from memory.
Scenario: integrated webshops cover about 60% of order lines; the rest go by e-mail or phone.
Manager and office time is outside the supervisor's savings.

Input contract for s1: stock on hand in the stock module from deliveries booked in at s7 and a weekly count of key items by the kitchen team; the shortage report is computed from that and the par levels.
unknowns: Whether contract prices are agreed with suppliers.
research_questions: How often do invoice prices differ from agreed prices today?

already_counted.description: Supervisor reviews and adjusts the order proposal before it is sent.

incremental.description: Supervisor fixes failed webshop orders and updates article links.
Manager keeps par levels and contract prices current.
Kitchen team counts key items weekly into the stock module.

approvals.approved_version: Equipment requisition with item, supplier and price as approved in s5; a different item or higher price needs a new approval.
Order lines, quantities and suppliers as chosen by the supervisor in s2; edits after that need a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Kitchens that buy mostly from small local suppliers by phone keep most ordering and price-checking by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Handle group and party bookings: check dates, agree menu and numbers, quote, confirm and brief the team.

steps.what: Guest or company asks about parties or group reservations
Supervisor checks room, table and staff availability for the date
Supervisor discusses menu, numbers, budget, timing and diets with the guest
Supervisor writes the party quote with menu, price and terms
Guest accepts the quote, sometimes after changes
Supervisor checks the accepted quote against the reviewed version
Supervisor schedules the party in the reservations system
Supervisor sends the booking confirmation to the guest
Supervisor writes the event sheet for kitchen and service team
Supervisor confirms final numbers and diets with the guest before the party

tasks.design: An online group enquiry form in the reservation system ({OTHER}) captures date, numbers, budget and dietary counts and shows availability; a quote generator in {DOCS} builds the offer from party packages with prices, which the supervisor adjusts for custom wishes. Once the supervisor has checked the accepted version, the booking is created and the confirmation sent automatically, the event sheet is generated from the booking, and the guest updates final numbers through a link with an automatic reminder.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each party was a thread of calls and e-mails, with the quote and event sheet typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Reservation systems offer group forms and confirmations, and quote templates fill from package data.
tasks.still_hard: Custom menus and nervous hosts need conversation; guests often change numbers late.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding what makes the occasion special and suggesting what will work in the room.

ambition.what: Companies booking small team events online outside opening hours, with a quote the same evening.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor talks with guests and adjusts quotes instead of typing them; booking terms stay theirs to set.

reach.learn: Whether group enquiries can share the online form.

evidence.claim: Reservation systems can take group enquiries online and send confirmations.
Guests must get information on the 14 EU allergens.
Under the hospitality collective agreement, on-call staff can be called 24 hours ahead, while the law says 4 days.
Dietary needs linked to named guests are health data; counts per table avoid that.

assumptions: Boundary: from the enquiry to final numbers passed to the kitchen; running the party is outside.

Input contract: party packages with menu, price per person and terms kept by the restaurant manager; enquiry fields filled by the guest online or by the supervisor on the phone; fallback is the e-mail thread.
Diets are collected as counts per type, not per named guest.
Guest time is priced as customer time, not as the supervisor's savings.
unknowns: How many party enquiries arrive per week and through which channel.
Whether the reservation system supports group forms.
research_questions: Do online enquiries convert to bookings as often as phone enquiries?

already_counted.description: Supervisor checks the generated quote and adjusts it for custom wishes.
Supervisor checks the generated event sheet before it goes to the team.

incremental.description: Supervisor answers questions about online enquiries and fixes failed confirmations.
Manager keeps party packages, prices and terms current.
Guests fill in the online enquiry form and update final numbers through the link instead of phoning.

approvals.approved_version: The quote as accepted by the guest and checked by the supervisor in s6; a changed quote needs a new check.
The quote as accepted by the guest and checked by the supervisor in s6; the confirmation states only that version.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Restaurants whose party guests mostly phone and ask for custom menus keep long conversations and edited quotes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set the department's objectives and budget, and write or update its policies and procedures.

steps.what: Supervisor gathers sales, labour cost, food cost and waste figures
Supervisor drafts departmental objectives and the budget in a spreadsheet
Supervisor writes or updates policies and procedures, such as the allergen procedure

loop.input: The supervisor's bullet points on what changes, the current procedure and the required elements list from the hygiene code.
loop.output: A revised procedure in the house format with numbered steps.
loop.check: Every required element on the list must appear; temperatures, times and quantities must match the hygiene code values or the current procedure; a diff shows every change for the supervisor to accept.
loop.stop: Two redrafts at most; then the supervisor edits by hand. The manager approves before use.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning bullets into clear procedure text needs writing; a template only holds headings.

steps.what: Supervisor discusses the draft budget and procedures with the manager
Restaurant manager approves the budget, objectives and procedures
Supervisor publishes the approved plan and procedures and explains them to the team

tasks.design: A monthly {BI} view joins till sales, roster hours, food cost from the recipe and stock system and waste data, and pre-fills next period's budget template with last year's actuals and forecast covers. Procedures are revised by a bounded model step from the supervisor's bullets, checked against the hygiene code's required elements, and published in {DOCS} only after the manager's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures sat in the till, rosters and spreadsheets, and procedures were text documents rewritten from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe, till and roster data can feed one dashboard, waste can be measured, and language models draft procedure text that a checklist can verify.
tasks.still_hard: Setting targets and policies is judgement and negotiation with the manager and team.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing targets the team believes in and writing rules people actually follow.

ambition.what: Food cost, labour and waste reviewed monthly against targets, not once a year at budget time.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor sets targets and reviews drafts instead of collecting figures; the manager approves from consistent material.

reach.task: Set food cost and waste targets for the kitchen
reach.learn: Whether waste data per dish changes the chef's menu choices.

evidence.claim: A hotel cut food waste by 33% in under 12 months, 3,300 kg and EUR 27,000, from waste-tracking data.
A recipe tool adds labour to ingredient cost for a prime cost per dish.
Food businesses need a HACCP plan, met through the approved hygiene code.
In 2022 only 41% of inspected hospitality businesses complied with allergen information rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from gathering figures to approved plans and procedures shared with the team.

Input contract: till sales per day, roster hours from the scheduling system, food cost from the recipe and stock system, waste weights if measured; required elements list kept by the manager from the hygiene code; fallback is spreadsheets.
The dashboard shows department totals, not individual staff.
Manager time is outside the supervisor's savings.

Input contract for s1: closing stock from the monthly count the kitchen team already does, entered in the stock system instead of on the stock sheet; waste only where it is weighed, so waste figures stay partly estimated and s1 keeps 40%.
unknowns: Whether roster hours and food cost can be exported.
research_questions: Do monthly reviews against targets change food cost within a year?

already_counted.description: Supervisor checks dashboard figures before using them in the budget.
Supervisor checks drafted procedures against practice and accepts each change.

incremental.description: Supervisor keeps the required elements list and budget template current.
Finance or IT keeps the data feeds and model service running.

approvals.approved_version: Budget, objectives and procedure texts as approved by the manager in s5; any later edit needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where rosters or food cost cannot be exported, the supervisor keeps building figures by hand; procedure revisions are rare in a stable kitchen.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The supervisor checks estimates, proposals, quotes and drafts instead of producing them; conversations with guests, staff and the manager stay.
reach: Chefs' recipe data and waste targets
skills_to_grow: Keeping recipe and package data accurate
Reviewing generated orders and quotes critically
Reading cost and waste figures to set targets
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who runs purchasing and parties from checked proposals and reviews cost, labour and waste every month.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
